core.title: BodySync AI: A Multimodal Agentic System for Nutrition Label Extraction and Pose-Based Body Analysis
core.abstract: This paper presents BodySync AI, a multimodal calorie-tracking prototype that combines optical character recognition (OCR), object detection, pose estimation, and an agentic large language model (LLM). The system supports two tasks: extracting nutritional values from photographs of food-packaging labels, and analyzing body proportions from full-body images. Nutrition extraction uses a classical image-processing front end (perspective correction, denoising, illumination normalization, and contrast enhancement) followed by EasyOCR and rulebased parsing of calories, fat, carbohydrates, and protein. In parallel, we train a YOLOv8n nutrition-label detector on the Open Food Facts Nutrition Table Detection dataset and study the effect of training epochs, learning rate, optimizer, batch size, and input resolution in 14 controlled runs. The best configuration reaches an mAP@50 of 0.904 and an mAP@50-95 of 0.727 on the validation split. Body analysis uses MediaPipe Pose landmarks to compute normalized shoulder width, hip width, torso length, and shoulder-to-hip ratio, which feed a baseline rule-based bodytype estimate. A Groq-hosted Llama 3.1 8B agent exposes these components as tools through a natural-language interface. We describe the system as built, report the detector experiments, and outline the evaluations and learned body-composition models planned as future work.

core.title_zh: BodySync AI：用于营养标签提取与基于姿态的身体分析的多模态智能体系统

article.lead: 如何让一个系统同时读取食品营养标签、分析身体比例，并通过自然语言提供访问入口？BodySync AI 将图像处理与大语言模型智能体组合成原型，为理解多模态工具如何协同提供了一个具体案例。

sections.title: 从食品标签到身体比例的两个任务
paragraphs: BodySync AI 是一个多模态卡路里追踪原型，结合光学字符识别、目标检测、姿态估计和智能体式大语言模型。系统面向两类输入：食品包装标签照片与全身图像，分别用于提取营养数值和分析身体比例。

sections.title: 识别、检测与姿态工具如何组合
paragraphs: 营养信息提取先进行透视校正、去噪、光照归一化和对比度增强，再使用 EasyOCR 和基于规则的解析，提取卡路里、脂肪、碳水化合物及蛋白质信息。
与此同时，研究者使用 Open Food Facts Nutrition Table Detection 数据集训练 YOLOv8n 营养标签检测器，通过 14 次受控运行研究训练轮数、学习率、优化器、批量大小和输入分辨率的影响。
身体分析使用 MediaPipe Pose 关键点计算归一化肩宽、臀宽、躯干长度和肩臀比，并据此进行基于规则的基线体型估计。由 Groq 托管的 Llama 3.1 8B 智能体则通过自然语言界面，将这些组件作为工具提供。

sections.title: 检测器在验证集上的报告结果
paragraphs: 摘要报告，最佳检测器配置在验证集上的 mAP@50 为 0.904，mAP@50-95 为 0.727。这是营养标签检测器的结果，不能直接代表营养数值提取、体型估计或整个系统的准确程度。
作者介绍了已构建的系统并报告检测器实验；摘要同时将相关评估和基于学习的身体成分模型列为未来工作，而非已完成成果。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能回答哪些验证问题
paragraphs: 摘要未报告数据集的样本规模、验证集构成，也未给出不同配置的逐项比较结果，因此仅凭摘要无法判断结果对不同标签、拍摄条件或人群的适用范围。
摘要也未给出营养提取和身体分析的具体评估指标，无法据此判断两项任务及自然语言交互的实际表现；这并不意味着论文一定没有开展相关分析。

paragraphs: 阅读启发：这个原型值得从“智能体如何调用专门工具”与“各工具的结果如何验证”两个层面理解。进一步阅读时，可关注检测器配置之间的比较，以及营养提取、身体分析和系统整体评估的具体范围。

core.title: TKG-Thinker: Towards Dynamic Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs via Agentic Reinforcement Learning
core.abstract: Temporal knowledge graph question answering (TKGQA) aims to answer time-sensitive questions by leveraging temporal knowledge bases. While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in TKGQA, current prompting strategies constrain their efficacy in two primary ways. First, they are prone to reasoning hallucinations under complex temporal constraints. Second, static prompting limits model autonomy and generalization, as it lacks optimization through dynamic interaction with temporal knowledge graph (TKG) environments. To address these limitations, we propose TKG-Thinker, a novel agent equipped with autonomous planning and adaptive retrieval capabilities for reasoning over TKGs. Specifically, TKG-Thinker performs in-depth temporal reasoning through dynamic multi-turn interactions with TKGs via a dual-training strategy. We first apply Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with chain of thought data to instill core planning capabilities, followed by a Reinforcement Learning (RL) stage that leverages multi-dimensional rewards to refine reasoning policies under intricate temporal constraints. Experimental results on benchmark datasets with three open-source LLMs show that TKG-Thinker achieves state-of-the-art performance and exhibits strong generalization across complex TKGQA settings.

deep_read.problem: 论文关注时序知识图谱问答中实体关系与时间约束的联合推理。作者指出，现有方法可能在问题分解时忽略前后或先后条件，产生推理幻觉；静态、人工设计的工作流也限制了模型通过环境交互检查和修正证据的能力。[P1][P2]
deep_read.method: 方法将知识图谱作为动态环境，先使用经过格式和答案正确性过滤的教师轨迹进行监督微调，为规划与工具调用提供初始化；再通过在线强化学习优化策略。动作包括思考、规划、时间检索和回答，奖励结合格式、检索覆盖及最终答案正确性。[P3][P4][P5]
deep_read.innovation: 作者的方法特点是将时序问答组织为规划、思考、工具调用和观察交替进行的决策过程，并把严格早于、严格晚于和区间查询等时间操作显式纳入动作空间。监督冷启动与多维奖励共同服务于这一交互流程；其首创性仍以作者自身表述为限。[P2][P5]
deep_read.findings: 作者报告，相对最强基线，两个主基准的总体 Hits@1 分别提高 7.60 和 7.30 个百分点。MULTITQ 消融中，完整模型为 0.855，移除监督微调、规划或替换时间检索器后分别降至 0.591、0.796 和 0.458；跨域表格中的最佳总体结果也高于所列基线。[P6][P7][P14]
deep_read.limitations: 作者指出奖励主要依靠二元指标和规则，难以细致评估中间推理，现有基准的推理跳数也有限。解读：案例中还出现无关思考及事件方向、时间条件不一致，正确答案不等于全过程可靠。本批笔记未记录经原页核实的原文件缺项，不能据此补造缺失公式或其影响。[P9][P18][P19][P20]
deep_read.connection: 解读：时间约束检索、证据追踪与多步规划可为智能运维中的事件关联或历史状态查询提供方法参照；时间对齐也可能启发可靠性记录分析。但本文实验是通用时序知识图谱问答，资料未提供结构设计或工业运维验证，不能直接推断实际应用效果。[P5][P6][P14]
deep_read.next_steps: 建议先构建具有明确时间戳、事件方向和可追溯证据的领域问答集，再比较纯语义检索与时间约束检索，并单独评估中间步骤的逻辑一致性。对于长链任务，可设置更复杂多跳和开放世界测试；这些是迁移研究设想，而非论文已验证的成果。[P7][P9][P19]

core.title: TimelineAgent: An LLM-based Framework for Query-Centric Event Timeline Extraction Across Multiple Documents
core.abstract: Query-centric cross-document event timeline extraction aims to construct event timelines from multiple documents under diverse query focuses. The task is very challenging due to the heterogeneous event modeling and reasoning requirements arising from both the intrinsic complexity of cross-document timeline construction and the diversity of query focuses. In this paper, we propose TimelineAgent, an LLM-based multi-agent framework featuring a multi-stage reasoning workflow, where heterogeneous event features are organized into reusable skills and orchestrated through a goal-oriented protocol. To facilitate evaluation, we construct a benchmark covering diverse query focuses. Experimental results show that TimelineAgent consistently outperforms existing methods, offering a practical framework for complex real-world timeline construction.

core.title: Time is Not a Label: Continuous Phase Rotation for Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Agentic Memory
core.abstract: Structured memory representations such as knowledge graphs are central to autonomous agents and other long-lived systems. However, most existing approaches model time as discrete metadata, either sorting by recency (burying old-yet-permanent knowledge), simply overwriting outdated facts, or requiring an expensive LLM call at every ingestion step, leaving them unable to distinguish persistent facts from evolving ones. To address this, we introduce RoMem, a drop-in temporal knowledge graph module for structured memory systems, applicable to agentic memory and beyond. A pretrained Semantic Speed Gate maps each relation’s text embedding to a volatility score, learning from data that evolving relations (e.g., “president of”) should rotate fast while persistent ones (e.g., “born in”) should remain stable. Combined with continuous phase rotation, this enables geometric shadowing: obsolete facts are rotated out of phase in complex vector space, so temporally correct facts naturally outrank contradictions without deletion. On temporal knowledge graph completion, RoMem achieves state-of-the-art results on ICEWS05-15 (72.6 MRR). Applied to agentic memory, it delivers 2-3x MRR and answer accuracy on temporal reasoning (MultiTQ), dominates hybrid benchmark (LoCoMo), preserves static memory with zero degradation (DMR-MSC), and generalises zero-shot to unseen financial domains (FinTMMBench).

core.title: TIDE: Trajectory-based Diagnostic Evaluation of Test-Time Improvement in LLM Agents
core.abstract: Recent advances in autonomous LLM agents demonstrate their ability to improve performance through iterative interaction with the environment. We define this paradigm as Test-Time Improvement (TTI). However, the mechanisms under how and why TTI succeed or fail remain poorly understood, and existing evaluation metrics fail to capture their task optimization efficiency, behavior adaptation after erroneous actions, and the specific utility of working memory. To address these gaps, we propose Test-time Improvement Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), a lightweight, agent-agnostic and environment-agnostic framework that decomposes TTI into three comprehensive and interconnected dimensions. The framework measures (1) the overall temporal dynamics of task completion and (2) identifies whether performance is constrained by recursive looping behaviors or (3) by burdensome accumulated memory. Through extensive experiments, TIDE highlights that improving agent performance calls for explicitly optimizing the interaction dynamics between the agent and the environment.

core.title: The Consistency Illusion: How Multi-Agent Debate Hides Reasoning Misalignment
core.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems for medical question answering treat consensus as a reliability signal: if multiple agents agree on an answer, it is presumed trustworthy. However, answer-level consensus does not entail reasoning-level alignment. We introduce CARA (Cross-Agent Reasoning Alignment), a family of automated metrics that measure whether agents who agree on an answer also agree on the reasoning. Applying CARA to a standard debate system on two medical QA benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE and MedThink-Bench), we identify the consistency illusion: a failure mode where debate reduces detectable contradictions between agents while simultaneously decreasing the semantic similarity of their reasoning chains; agents appear to agree more but reason less consistently. To improve this misalignment, we propose the Grounded Debate Protocol (GDP), a prompt-level intervention that requires agents to commit to named medical facts and take explicit stances on other agents’ claims. GDP produces large, consistent alignment improvements (Cohen’s d = +1.43 to +1.99) across two datasets and two backbone models, without adding LLM calls or modifying system architecture. Our results motivate cross-agent reasoning alignment as a quantity to audit alongside accuracy in safety-critical domains.

papers.title: BodySync AI: A Multimodal Agentic System for Nutrition Label Extraction and Pose-Based Body Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper presents BodySync AI, a multimodal calorie-tracking prototype that combines optical character recognition (OCR), object detection, pose estimation, and an agentic large language model (LLM). The system supports two tasks: extracting nutritional values from photographs of food-packaging labels, and analyzing body proportions from full-body images. Nutrition extraction uses a classical image-processing front end (perspective correction, denoising, illumination normalization, and contrast enhancement) followed by EasyOCR and rulebased parsing of calories, fat, carbohydrates, and protein. In parallel, we train a YOLOv8n nutrition-label detector on the Open Food Facts Nutrition Table Detection dataset and study the effect of training epochs, learning rate, optimizer, batch size, and input resolution in 14 controlled runs. The best configuration reaches an mAP@50 of 0.904 and an mAP@50-95 of 0.727 on the validation split. Body analysis uses MediaPipe Pose landmarks to compute normalized shoulder width, hip width, torso length, and shoulder-to-hip ratio, which feed a baseline rule-based bodytype estimate. A Groq-hosted Llama 3.1 8B agent exposes these components as tools through a natural-language interface. We describe the system as built, report the detector experiments, and outline the evaluations and learned body-composition models planned as future work.

papers.title: TKG-Thinker: Towards Dynamic Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs via Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Temporal knowledge graph question answering (TKGQA) aims to answer time-sensitive questions by leveraging temporal knowledge bases. While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in TKGQA, current prompting strategies constrain their efficacy in two primary ways. First, they are prone to reasoning hallucinations under complex temporal constraints. Second, static prompting limits model autonomy and generalization, as it lacks optimization through dynamic interaction with temporal knowledge graph (TKG) environments. To address these limitations, we propose TKG-Thinker, a novel agent equipped with autonomous planning and adaptive retrieval capabilities for reasoning over TKGs. Specifically, TKG-Thinker performs in-depth temporal reasoning through dynamic multi-turn interactions with TKGs via a dual-training strategy. We first apply Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with chain of thought data to instill core planning capabilities, followed by a Reinforcement Learning (RL) stage that leverages multi-dimensional rewards to refine reasoning policies under intricate temporal constraints. Experimental results on benchmark datasets with three open-source LLMs show that TKG-Thinker achieves state-of-the-art performance and exhibits strong generalization across complex TKGQA settings.

deep_read.innovation: 作者的方法特点是将时序问答组织为规划、思考、工具调用和观察交替进行的决策过程，并把严格早于、严格晚于和区间查询等时间操作显式纳入动作空间。监督冷启动与多维奖励共同服务于这一交互流程；其首创性仍以作者自身表述为限。[P2][P5]

papers.title: TimelineAgent: An LLM-based Framework for Query-Centric Event Timeline Extraction Across Multiple Documents
papers.abstract: Query-centric cross-document event timeline extraction aims to construct event timelines from multiple documents under diverse query focuses. The task is very challenging due to the heterogeneous event modeling and reasoning requirements arising from both the intrinsic complexity of cross-document timeline construction and the diversity of query focuses. In this paper, we propose TimelineAgent, an LLM-based multi-agent framework featuring a multi-stage reasoning workflow, where heterogeneous event features are organized into reusable skills and orchestrated through a goal-oriented protocol. To facilitate evaluation, we construct a benchmark covering diverse query focuses. Experimental results show that TimelineAgent consistently outperforms existing methods, offering a practical framework for complex real-world timeline construction.

papers.title: Time is Not a Label: Continuous Phase Rotation for Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Agentic Memory
papers.abstract: Structured memory representations such as knowledge graphs are central to autonomous agents and other long-lived systems. However, most existing approaches model time as discrete metadata, either sorting by recency (burying old-yet-permanent knowledge), simply overwriting outdated facts, or requiring an expensive LLM call at every ingestion step, leaving them unable to distinguish persistent facts from evolving ones. To address this, we introduce RoMem, a drop-in temporal knowledge graph module for structured memory systems, applicable to agentic memory and beyond. A pretrained Semantic Speed Gate maps each relation’s text embedding to a volatility score, learning from data that evolving relations (e.g., “president of”) should rotate fast while persistent ones (e.g., “born in”) should remain stable. Combined with continuous phase rotation, this enables geometric shadowing: obsolete facts are rotated out of phase in complex vector space, so temporally correct facts naturally outrank contradictions without deletion. On temporal knowledge graph completion, RoMem achieves state-of-the-art results on ICEWS05-15 (72.6 MRR). Applied to agentic memory, it delivers 2-3x MRR and answer accuracy on temporal reasoning (MultiTQ), dominates hybrid benchmark (LoCoMo), preserves static memory with zero degradation (DMR-MSC), and generalises zero-shot to unseen financial domains (FinTMMBench).

papers.title: TIDE: Trajectory-based Diagnostic Evaluation of Test-Time Improvement in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in autonomous LLM agents demonstrate their ability to improve performance through iterative interaction with the environment. We define this paradigm as Test-Time Improvement (TTI). However, the mechanisms under how and why TTI succeed or fail remain poorly understood, and existing evaluation metrics fail to capture their task optimization efficiency, behavior adaptation after erroneous actions, and the specific utility of working memory. To address these gaps, we propose Test-time Improvement Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), a lightweight, agent-agnostic and environment-agnostic framework that decomposes TTI into three comprehensive and interconnected dimensions. The framework measures (1) the overall temporal dynamics of task completion and (2) identifies whether performance is constrained by recursive looping behaviors or (3) by burdensome accumulated memory. Through extensive experiments, TIDE highlights that improving agent performance calls for explicitly optimizing the interaction dynamics between the agent and the environment.

papers.title: The Consistency Illusion: How Multi-Agent Debate Hides Reasoning Misalignment
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems for medical question answering treat consensus as a reliability signal: if multiple agents agree on an answer, it is presumed trustworthy. However, answer-level consensus does not entail reasoning-level alignment. We introduce CARA (Cross-Agent Reasoning Alignment), a family of automated metrics that measure whether agents who agree on an answer also agree on the reasoning. Applying CARA to a standard debate system on two medical QA benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE and MedThink-Bench), we identify the consistency illusion: a failure mode where debate reduces detectable contradictions between agents while simultaneously decreasing the semantic similarity of their reasoning chains; agents appear to agree more but reason less consistently. To improve this misalignment, we propose the Grounded Debate Protocol (GDP), a prompt-level intervention that requires agents to commit to named medical facts and take explicit stances on other agents’ claims. GDP produces large, consistent alignment improvements (Cohen’s d = +1.43 to +1.99) across two datasets and two backbone models, without adding LLM calls or modifying system architecture. Our results motivate cross-agent reasoning alignment as a quantity to audit alongside accuracy in safety-critical domains.
